body: The layout engine every GuiOS screen is arranged by. `widget-layout` resolves a style, insets the container to a content box, turns each child into a `LayoutItem` and hands the list to `flex-layout`; `GuiShell`, `TrackerApp`, `DiffusionApp` and all six of the small guios apps reach it through `widget-layout`, `widget-set-flex` and `widget-set-min`.

body: The GuiOS golden frames DO exercise this, unlike the AppRunner frame loop next door, which is why it is asked second. What a golden cannot do is say WHICH rule produced a frame: a proportional split and an equal split of a two-child row differ by pixels a recorded image compares without interpreting. This chapter asks for the numbers.

body: The integration, driven as an app drives it. The parent's own bounds must be the container it was handed; the children are placed inside the content box, which the panel's theme padding and border inset. That inset is printed rather than predicted -- the point of this line is that the children land inside the parent and in order, and that a flexing child is wider than a fixed one.

author: reek
body: The inset and the label's own contribution, printed so the row above closes arithmetically instead of being taken on trust. The flexing child's width must be the content width less the fixed child's OUTER width, and the outer width is the declared minimum plus whatever margin the theme resolves for a label. Without these two the tree row is a number nobody can check.
